name: UH-1Y Venom
summary: Marine Corps twin-engine utility helicopter that rebuilt the Huey with the AH-1Z's four-blade rotor, engines and tail, used for troop lift, escort and command and control.

wings: No stub wings; weapons are door guns or side-mounted rocket pods
engines: Two engines on the cabin roof with large exhausts angled up and outward
Taller, bulkier engine fairing than older twin Hueys
fuselage: Classic Huey cabin, stretched, with large sliding doors
Longer nose with a FLIR sensor ball under the tip
tail: Four-blade tail rotor at the top of the fin
Small horizontal stabilizers on the tail boom

tellTales: Classic boxy utility cabin on skids, but with a four-blade main rotor and four-blade tail rotor
Sensor ball under an extended nose
Large up-angled twin exhausts on the roof

confusedWith.howToTell: The Venom has a four-blade tail rotor, a longer nose with a FLIR ball and military gray paint; the civil 412 keeps a two-blade tail rotor and a plain nose.
The Venom has four main rotor blades and a four-blade tail rotor; the UH-1H/N and Bell 205/212 have a two-blade main rotor and two-blade tail rotor.
The Viper is a narrow tandem-seat gunship with stub wings; the Venom has a wide troop cabin with side-by-side pilots.
